summary: Add an opt-in admission boundary without changing the M11 SLO or the default submit path.
planned_actions: first inspect submit, cancellation, metrics, and M11 measurement paths without editing
add a focused regression proving rejected admission creates no job and consumes no id
implement the smallest opt-in admission check using the existing lifecycle authority path
keep default submit behavior unchanged when admission control is disabled
run focused tests, core tests, and applicable M04-M11 probes
produce a diff and evidence report for independent review
evidence_claims: rejected admission has zero job-state side effects
accepted jobs retain the existing lifecycle semantics
the M11 SLO target and denominator remain unchanged
open_questions: What exact public result/error shape should represent overload? The task contract says this is a compatibility decision that requires escalation if the existing boundary cannot express it without changing callers.
What capacity threshold should the opt-in policy use? The task contract intentionally does not authorize inventing a product threshold.
